_comment: Numbers in prose, pinned to a resolver that re-derives them from the repository.
Read by scripts/check-counts.mjs. Each entry names a document, a regex with exactly
one capture group around the number, a resolver, and why the number is worth guarding.
Two rules, matching scripts/catalog-known-defects.json and divergence-allowlist.json:
- an entry whose pattern matches nothing FAILS AS STALE, so a pin cannot outlive
- every occurrence of a pattern must agree, because a number repeated three times
is three chances to be wrong and '673-paper corpus' was exactly that.
Pin a number when being wrong about it would change a decision. Do not pin every
digit in the documentation — a pin file nobody can read is one nobody maintains.

claims.reason: The corpus is the stated warrant for the four measured results this ADR opens with. It said '673-paper corpus' three times; the tree holds 661 files and 599 unique documents. A warrant nobody can reproduce is not one.
Same claim, restated twice more in the corpus document itself — the place a reader would go to check it.
The file count and the document count differ by 62 byte-identical duplicates. Stating only one of them is how 599 got rounded up to 673.
This comment justifies ignoring the corpus. It said 906 MB against a measured 2,081 — the same drift class as the documentation, in a file that changes behaviour.
Said 180; the registry holds 195. check:plan already reports 195, so the repository knew and the ADR did not.
Action item 7 sizes future work off this number.
The 'catalog is a hypothesis space' argument counts the hypotheses.
The status table is the first thing a reader trusts.

claims.pattern: records behind a pure registry — ([\d,]+) frozen
claims.reason: 172 frozen records, from the frozen catalog rather than from memory.
Said 8 added; 23 were. The gap between 172 and 195 is exactly what this number is supposed to explain.
The plan's PROSE contradicted the plan's own machine-checked JSON block, which check:plan reads instead. Two claims, one document, one checker covering only one of them.
Same sentence, second wrong number.
Same sentence, third number — and the one check:plan's JSON block gets right, which is what makes the prose contradiction worth catching.

ADR-0008 names this partition 'the routing rule' deciding which cases may reach a judge. A stale partition is a stale rule, not a cosmetic count — this is the single highest-consequence number in the documentation.
The judge-routed share grew 25% (8 to 10) while the documented figure stood still. Judge calls are the expensive, biased path the rule exists to bound.
Completes the partition. Three numbers that must sum to the catalog size, checked separately so the sum cannot hide a compensating error.
True today, and pinned deliberately: a pin file containing only broken claims proves the checker fires, never that it stays quiet when it should.
Second currently-true pin, in a different document, for the same must-not-fire reason.
CLAUDE.md is loaded into every session, so a wrong number here misleads before any file is read. It said 26; there are 31.
Third currently-true pin. Also the number CLAUDE.md is most likely to be trusted on without checking.
